title: Grade meshes bound to a second skin in the rig gate
body:
## Summary
parseGlbRig leaves out any mesh a node binds to a skin other than skins[0], so its weights are never graded.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/rig-gate.ts:212 keeps only meshes bound to skin 0 or to no skin, and jointCount/jointNames come from skins[0] alone. Before this round such a mesh was unread as well; the round made the exclusion explicit rather than fixing it. Fixed means one set of facts per skin, or a warning that names how many meshes went ungraded.

## Flow
- GLB with two skins -> gateRig
- the mesh on skins[1] is skipped
- verdict covers only skins[0]

## Expected impact
Multi-skin characters stop passing on a partial reading. Could break consumers that assume one jointNames list.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate covers every skin
Before: mesh on skins[1] with an unweighted vertex: zeroWeightVertices 0 (pinned by a test this round)
After: not built; predicted zeroWeightVertices 1 or a named ungraded-mesh warning
Method: simulation - RigFacts shape is single-skin and consumers (rig-check.ts, skintokens-runner.ts) were not reworked in this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: skinnedGlb fixture with two skins plus a count of real multi-skin GLBs under generated/

title: Rig weight tolerance cannot survive the quantization it claims to
body:
## Summary
WEIGHT_SUM_TOLERANCE is 1e-3 and its comment says it survives 8/16-bit quantization, but one 8-bit step is 3.9e-3.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/rig-gate.ts:325. A vertex summing to 254/255 fails as not normalized. glTF asks exporters to normalize exactly, so whether to widen is a real choice: a per-encoding tolerance keeps floats strict. Fixed means either a tolerance derived from the weight encoding or a comment that stops claiming this.

## Flow
- 8-bit weights summing 254/255 -> scoreRig
- failure: weights are not normalized

## Expected impact
Removes a possible false fail on 8-bit exporters; widening could admit genuinely sloppy rigs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - comment and threshold agree
Before: scoreRig with weightSumMin 254/255: pass false (probe)
After: not built
Method: probe - before figure taken; no real 8-bit GLB exists in the fixtures to show the case occurs
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: count of 8-bit-weight GLBs under generated/ and their weight-sum spread

title: View critique reads a punctuated none as a defect
body:
## Summary
parseViewCritiqueReply has the sentinel defect fixed in reference-conformance this round.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/view-critique.ts:119 tests /^none$/i, so DEFECTS=None. yields the defect list ["None."]. The file belongs to a sibling context this wave.

## Flow
- vision replies DEFECTS=None.; SEVERITY=0
- defects ["None."]

## Expected impact
A clean view stops carrying a phantom defect. Nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - same sentinel rule in both parsers
Before: reference-conformance fixed (test red then green); view-critique unchanged
After: same one-character regex change
Method: gate - proven on the twin parser; this file is out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Mixamo finger bones never conform onto UE5 names
body:
## Summary
planConform maps 0 of 5 Mixamo finger bones to UE5 names, though ue5-mannequin declares hasFingers true.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/bone-conform.ts:99 tokens() keeps the hand word, so LeftHandThumb1 has stem handthumb while thumb_01_l has stem thumb; the groups never meet. src/lib/visual-gen/rig-presets.ts:54 declares fingers, its mapping has zero finger rows, and chain binding checks endpoints only, so the gate cannot see it. A character that must grip passes binding with no driven fingers.

## Flow
- planConform of mixamorig:LeftHand{Thumb,Index,Middle,Ring,Pinky}1 onto thumb_01_l etc.
- coverage 0

## Expected impact
Grip animation retargets. Synonyms are a known way to map a bone wrongly, so each needs a pinned pair.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - finger coverage
Before: coverage 0 of 5 (probe)
After: predicted 5 of 5 after a hand-prefix rule for finger stems
Method: probe - before only; the after needs the rule built and checked against all three vocabularies
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: planConform coverage over full Mixamo, UE5 and Tripo finger lists

title: Two bone-name tokenizers disagree on vendor prefixes
body:
## Summary
skeleton-profiles and bone-conform each tokenize joint names with a different prefix rule.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/skeleton-profiles.ts:171 strips only mixamorig (and its classifier at line 194 does not treat mixamorig1 as Mixamo); src/lib/visual-gen/bone-conform.ts:74 strips mixamorig\d*, tripo, armature and root. This round fixed the numbered-namespace symptom in one copy. Fixed means one tokenizer, or a test that runs both over the same names.

## Flow
- tripo_Hips -> bone-conform drops the prefix; skeleton-profiles keeps tripo as a token
- the two modules read one name differently

## Expected impact
One rule for the gate and the conform. Classifying mixamorig1 as mixamo would route it to the table path, which matches exact names and would unbind it, so the change needs care.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one prefix rule
Before: 2 tokenizers with different prefix sets
After: 1 shared tokenizer
Method: simulation - walked mixamorig1, tripo_ and Armature_ names through both by reading
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: one table of real joint names run through both tokenizers

title: MetaHuman results cannot say the run never started
body:
## Summary
ConformResult and AssembleResult have no notRun, unlike ClothResult from the same runner.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/metahuman-conform.ts:78 has ok/error only. ExperimentResult.refused (live editor, drain lease) arrives as an ordinary failure, while chaos-cloth.ts keeps a machine state apart from a verdict on the asset.

## Flow
- editor busy -> runner refuses
- conform returns ok false with no way to tell it was never attempted

## Expected impact
A busy machine stops reading as a bad mesh, once something calls this seam.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - not-run is distinct from failed
Before: 0 of 2 MetaHuman results carry notRun; ClothResult does
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - no production caller exists to show the difference
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: runExperimentFn stub returning refused:true, once a caller exists

title: Chaos Cloth authors and saves assets after the garment failed
body:
## Summary
buildClothGraphPython carries on with _garment NONE, creating and saving a Dataflow and a ClothAsset.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/chaos-cloth.ts:96-123 logs the failed import, then still calls create_asset twice and saves. The result is correctly ok:false, but the assets stay on disk under /Game. Fixed means stopping after the garment marker when it is NONE.

## Flow
- garment glb import yields nothing
- POF_CLOTH_GARMENT=NONE
- DF_Cloth and CA_Cloth are still created

## Expected impact
No orphan assets from failed attaches. Needs an editor run to confirm the early exit keeps the marker contract.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed attach leaves nothing behind
Before: generated Python has no guard between the marker and create_asset (read)
After: not built
Method: simulation - proving it needs a UE editor run, which this round must not start
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: editor run with a garment path that fails import, then list /Game/Generated/Cloth

title: Linear-prop scope limit counts articles the comment excludes
body:
## Summary
SCOPE_WORD_LIMIT is documented as four content words, but articles are counted.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/linear-prop-routing.ts:31 says content words; line 73 counts every word. "a long hemp rope" is procedural and "the old frayed hemp rope" only advises, although both are one rope. Either the comment changes or stopwords are dropped, and that moves the refuse/advise boundary.

## Flow
- the old frayed hemp rope -> 5 words
- route advise, so a credit is spent

## Expected impact
Fewer paid generations of a plain rope; dropping articles may refuse more scene prompts.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the rule matches its statement
Before: a long hemp rope: procedural; the old frayed hemp rope: advise (probe)
After: not built
Method: probe - before only; which boundary is right needs real prompts
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: replay logged generation prompts through both counting rules

title: MetaHuman conform seam has no production caller
body:
## Summary
conformMeshToMetaHuman and assembleMetaHuman are exported and tested, and nothing calls them.

## Description
A grep for both names across src and scripts (.ts, .tsx, .mjs), excluding tests, returns only src/lib/visual-gen/metahuman-conform.ts. Its module header presents it as the auto-rig bridge. Keeping it unwired, surfacing it (the chaos-cloth route is the model), or removing it is a product decision.

## Flow
- grep conformMeshToMetaHuman|assembleMetaHuman in src scripts, excluding __tests__
- 1 file: its own module

## Expected impact
The operator learns the MetaHuman path is script-less today; three fixes landed here this round are reachable only from tests until it is wired.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - capability is reachable
Before: 0 production callers (grep)
After: operator decides
Method: gate - grep is the measurement; the choice is not measurable
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Reference-role assembler has no production caller
body:
## Summary
assembleReferenceDirective, REFERENCE_ROLES, ROLE_IDS and getReferenceRole are used only inside their own module and its test.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/reference-roles.ts:173. GEN_PROMPTING_REACH already admits this for the practices list; the role scaffold has the same status and no such note. Line 181 also passes the label as a replace() string, so a $& in a label would be expanded; worth fixing only if this gets wired.

## Flow
- grep the four names in src scripts, excluding __tests__
- 1 file: its own module

## Expected impact
Wiring it would give generation prompts role tags; removing it drops about 40 lines.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - capability is reachable
Before: 0 production callers (grep)
After: operator decides
Method: gate - grep is the measurement; the choice is not measurable
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: MetaHuman conform assumes the first imported object is the mesh
body:
## Summary
buildConformPython loads imported_object_paths[0] as the conform target.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/metahuman-conform.ts:57 takes _paths[0]. A textured GLB imports materials and textures too, and nothing here shows the mesh sorts first. The header's ground-truth run does not state whether its GLB was textured.

## Flow
- textured glb imported
- load_asset(_paths[0]) may be a material
- get_mesh_data_for_conforming fails

## Expected impact
A wrong-target failure gets a clear reason, or the assumption gets confirmed.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the target is really the mesh
Before: unknown; no editor run this round
After: select the first StaticMesh from the imported paths
Method: simulation - operator-only: needs a UE 5.8 editor with the MetaHuman plugin
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: one headless conform of a textured GLB, logging imported_object_paths
